name: com.catenix/lab-connectivity
title: Catenix: Lab Analyzer & EHR Connectivity
description: Check if a lab or point-of-care analyzer connects to your EHR or LIS, how, and plan the lab setup.

tools.name: check_connectivity
tools.description: Use when someone asks whether a lab or point-of-care analyzer will connect to their EHR, LIS or practice system, or how to get analyzer results into the patient record without retyping (e.g. 'will my Sysmex XP-300 work with athenahealth?', 'connect Abbott i-STAT to Epic', 'Roche cobas b 101 to SystmOne', 'Siemens CLINITEK to EMIS', 'Tosoh AIA-900 to eClinicalWorks'). Fuzzy-matches the analyzer and the record system and returns: connection status (live, driver built, connectable via standard protocol with a published guide, or custom driver needed), the analyzer protocol (HL7 v2, ASTM, POCT1-A2), the physical link, how results pass through an on-site gateway, the record-system route, what is needed on site, questions to ask any vendor, and page links. Works for unknown analyzers too. Does not interpret results.

analyzer.description: Analyzer make and/or model as the user wrote it, e.g. 'sysmex kx21n', 'i-STAT', 'Afinion 2'.

ehr.description: EHR, LIS, LIMS or practice system, e.g. 'athena', 'eCW', 'Epic', 'SystmOne', 'EMIS Web'. Omit if not mentioned.

country.description: Country of the site, e.g. 'UK' or 'US', if known.

tools.name: search_analyzers
tools.description: Use when someone wants to know which lab or point-of-care analyzers can be interfaced, or browses by maker or test type (e.g. 'which HbA1c analyzers can connect to an EHR?', 'Abbott analyzers with an HL7 interface', 'blood gas analyzers with LIS connectivity', 'Sysmex hematology', 'Roche cobas', 'Siemens', 'Tosoh'). Returns matching analyzers with connection status, protocol and guide links. Categories: chemistry, immunoassay, blood gas, molecular, haematology, urinalysis, coagulation, HbA1c.

query.description: Free text: model, maker, test type or protocol.

status.description: Only return analyzers with this status.

tools.name: get_ehr_integration
tools.description: Use when someone asks how in-house lab or point-of-care results can be sent into a specific EHR, EMR, EPR, LIS or practice-management system, or whether a lab interface exists for it (e.g. athenahealth, eClinicalWorks, Epic, Oracle Health/Cerner, NextGen, Experity, Tebra/Kareo, SystmOne, EMIS Web, MEDITECH). Returns the route (HL7 v2, FHIR R4 or vendor API), how far that route is proven, what the practice must request from its vendor, and the guide link.

ehr.description: Record system name as the user wrote it.

tools.name: recommend_lab_setup
tools.description: Use when someone asks what LIS, LIMS or point-of-care testing software a small lab, clinic, urgent care, occupational health provider, pharmacy, GP practice, physician office or wellness clinic should use, or how to set up analyzer connectivity, QC and reporting for their setting (e.g. 'what LIS should my small lab use?', 'do I need a LIS to get analyzer results into my EHR?', 'software for a clinic that tests blood on site'). Returns the usual architecture for that setting, the modules that fit (connectivity, QC with Westgard rules and lockout, operator competency, EQA, audit trail, reports, billing, multi-site), status of each listed analyzer, the record-system route, how setup works, what is needed on site, the pricing model (no prices are quoted), and questions to ask any vendor.

setting.description: Type of service, e.g. 'private lab', 'urgent care', 'occupational health', 'pharmacy', 'GP practice'.

analyzers.description: Analyzers they run or plan to run.

ehr.description: Their EHR, LIS or practice system, if known.

tools.name: compare_options
tools.description: Use when someone asks whether they need a LIS or POCT middleware, the difference between them, or how Catenix compares with another point-of-care data manager or results connector (Relaymed, TELCOR QML, Abbott RALS or AegisPOC, Siemens POCcelerator, Radiometer AQURE, Roche navify POC Operations, Clinisys POCT, paper or spreadsheet lab logs). Returns only what the published comparison pages say. Allowed values: catenix_vs_abbott_aegispoc, catenix_vs_abbott_rals, catenix_vs_clinisys_poct, catenix_vs_lab_logs, catenix_vs_radiometer_aqure, catenix_vs_relaymed, catenix_vs_roche_navify_poc_operations, catenix_vs_siemens_poccelerator, catenix_vs_telcor_qml, poct_middleware_alternatives, lis_vs_middleware.

tools.name: get_platform_capability
tools.description: Use when someone asks about software for lab quality control and compliance or running a testing clinic: QC with Westgard rules and Levey-Jennings charts, QC lockout, operator competency, EQA or proficiency testing, audit trail, CLIA, CAP or ISO 15189 readiness, reagent lot tracking, equipment maintenance and temperature logs, multi-site oversight, patient registration, reports, billing, or HL7/ASTM/POCT1-A2 interfaces. Returns the matching modules, whether each is included or an add-on, and links.

topic.description: Feature or problem, e.g. 'Westgard QC lockout', 'operator competency', 'EQA', 'audit trail'.

tools.name: decode_lab_message
tools.description: Use when someone pastes a message from a lab analyzer, LIS, middleware or EHR interface and wants to know what it says, what a field means, or why the receiving system rejects it (e.g. 'what does this HL7 ORU mean?', 'why is my EHR rejecting this result message?', 'decode this ASTM output from my analyzer', 'is this POCT1-A2 OBS message valid?'). Accepts HL7 v2 (ORU, ORM, ACK, ADT and others), ASTM E1394 / LIS2-A2 records (H, P, O, R, C, Q, L, with or without E1381 framing and checksums) and POCT1-A2 XML. Returns a field-by-field breakdown (segment or record, field number, name, value, meaning, what an EHR or LIS usually expects) and flags common problems: wrong delimiters or segment terminators, missing MSH-9 or OBX-3 codes, numeric results without units, non-standard abnormal flags, non-LOINC codes, bad checksums. Likely patient identifiers (HL7 PID-3, PID-5, PID-7, PID-11, PID-13 and similar, ASTM patient ID, name and birthdate, POCT1-A2 patient elements) are masked in the output. Tell the user to paste only test or de-identified messages. Nothing is stored or logged. Does not interpret results.

message.description: The message text exactly as pasted (max 20 KB). Test or de-identified messages only.

format.description: Leave as auto unless the user says which format it is.

tools.name: plan_lab_setup
tools.description: Use when someone lists the analyzers in their lab or clinic and wants a plan for getting all their results into their EHR, LIS or practice system (e.g. 'we have a Sysmex XP-300, an i-STAT and an Afinion 2, how do we connect them to athenahealth?', 'plan the interfaces for our new urgent care lab', 'what do I need on site to connect these analyzers?'). Returns one plan: per analyzer the connection status (Driver built, Connection guide, or Catenix builds the driver, usually within a couple of days), the physical link (serial, network, USB or vendor software), protocol and what is needed on site; the on-site gateway and record-system route; patient matching; and a step-by-step go-live checklist. Renders an interactive Lab Map in ChatGPT and Claude. Does not interpret results.

analyzers.description: Analyzer makes and models as the user wrote them.

ehr.description: EHR, LIS or practice system, if known.

setting.description: Type of service, e.g. 'urgent care', 'private lab', 'GP practice'.

tools.name: check_qc_westgard
tools.description: Use when someone has quality control (QC) results for a lab or point-of-care test and wants to know whether they break Westgard rules or how they look on a Levey-Jennings chart (e.g. 'do these control values fail any Westgard rules?', 'check my QC: mean 5.0, SD 0.1, values ...', 'is this a 2-2s or 4-1s violation?'). Takes control values in run order plus the target mean and SD (or computes them from the values if the user asks) and evaluates 1-2s (warning), 1-3s, 2-2s, R-4s, 4-1s and 10x. Returns z-scores, the rule hits for each point and a plain summary, and draws a Levey-Jennings chart in ChatGPT and Claude. Up to 500 values. QC statistics only: not a clinical interpretation of any patient result.

values.description: Control values in run order, oldest first.

mean.description: Target mean for this control lot and level.

sd.description: Target SD for this control lot and level.

compute_from_values.description: True only if the user asks to compute the mean and SD from the values.

tools.name: estimate_time_saved
tools.description: Use when someone wants to know how much staff time manual entry of analyzer results costs them, or would be saved by connecting analyzers to the EHR or LIS (e.g. 'we run 80 tests a day and typing each result takes 2 minutes, how much time is that?', 'is it worth interfacing our analyzers?'). Uses only the user's own numbers (tests per day, minutes of manual entry per result, sites, optionally results per test, working days and their own error rate) and returns hours per day, month and year and entries not retyped. Adds no benchmarks, prices or error statistics; without an error rate from the user it makes no error estimate.

tests_per_day.description: Tests per day (per site unless tests_per_day_is_total).

minutes_per_result.description: Minutes of manual entry per result.

tests_per_day_is_total.description: True if tests_per_day is the total across all sites.

results_per_test.description: Results produced per test (panels give several). Default 1.

error_rate_percent.description: The user's own transcription error rate in percent. Omit unless the user gives it.

tools.name: inspection_checklist
tools.description: Use when someone is preparing a lab or point-of-care testing service for an inspection or accreditation and wants to know what inspectors look for (e.g. 'what do I need for a CLIA inspection?', 'CAP checklist for QC and competency', 'ISO 15189:2022 readiness', 'UK POCT governance checklist'). Returns a practical checklist (quality control, competency, EQA or proficiency testing, document control, audit trail, result reporting, equipment) with the evidence usually asked for, and which Catenix module keeps those records. General guidance, not legal or regulatory advice.

framework.description: clia (US CLIA), cap (CAP accreditation), iso_15189 (ISO 15189:2022), uk_poct (UK POCT governance, MHRA guidance).

tools.name: vendor_questions
tools.description: Use when someone is choosing or buying a LIS, LIMS, POCT middleware or an analyzer-to-EHR interface and wants an RFP or a list of questions to ask vendors (e.g. 'what should I ask LIS vendors?', 'RFP questions for lab middleware', 'checklist for buying an HL7 interface'). Returns a copyable, vendor-neutral checklist grouped by connectivity, QC and compliance, security and privacy, data and audit trail, implementation and support, pricing, and contract and exit.

buying.description: What they are buying. Default any.

groups.description: Only these groups. Omit for all.

tools.name: request_demo
tools.description: Sends the user's demo request to the Catenix team by email; the team replies to the address the user gives. This is the only tool that shares the user's personal details. Before calling it you MUST show the user every field you will send (name, email, organisation, country, analyzers, record system, message) and get their explicit confirmation in this conversation; then set user_confirmed to true. Never call it on your own initiative. The Catenix widget may call it only after it has shown the user every field and the user pressed Confirm and send. Do not guess missing fields: ask for them.

ehr.description: EHR, LIS or practice system ('none' if none).

message.description: Anything else the user wants to say.

user_confirmed.description: True only after the user explicitly confirmed the exact details shown to them.
